title: Set up Express sidecar server entry point
description: Create the Express sidecar server that runs separately from Next.js on port 3001. This gives Crawlee a proper Node.js runtime environment incompatible with Next.js Edge/Serverless. The server lives in src/scraper/ within the same repo.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/scraper/server.ts` starts an Express server on port 3001
Server logs 'Scraping API running on port 3001' on startup
Server handles errors gracefully without crashing
Running `tsx src/scraper/server.ts` starts the server successfully

steps.details: Create the following files (can be empty stubs for now): `src/scraper/server.ts`, `src/scraper/crawlee-service.ts`, `src/scraper/extract.ts`, `src/scraper/branding.ts`, `src/scraper/types.ts`

steps.description: Create src/scraper/types.ts with crawl request/response types

steps.details: Create Express server with JSON middleware, CORS enabled for localhost:3000. Register route handlers (stubs for now): POST /api/crawl and GET /api/health. Listen on port 3001. Add error handling middleware that returns `{ success: false, error: message }` with 500 status.

Run `npx tsx src/scraper/server.ts` in a terminal. Confirm 'Scraping API running on port 3001' is logged. In another terminal, run `curl http://localhost:3001/api/health` and confirm `{"status":"ok"}` is returned.

technicalNotes: The scraper server is not a separate package — it lives in src/scraper/ and uses the same node_modules as the Next.js app.
tsx is used to run TypeScript directly without a compile step: `tsx src/scraper/server.ts`
Port 3001 is hardcoded — if there's a conflict, it should be configurable via SCRAPER_PORT env var.
Do NOT import any Next.js or React dependencies in the scraper — it must be a pure Node.js/Express server.
